title: Salvaggio lineup: trumpets, trombone, drummers
summary: An eight-piece band; trumpeters included Rene LeWap and Walter Darwin, trombonist Chatelaine, drummers forgotten.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Yeah. So anyway, back to the line up in the band. He had one or two trumpets.
He had one trumpet. Yeah. Just one trumpet and I think one trombone. If I remember right, we had an eight piece band. I don't think we had a nine piece band. Let's see. An eight piece band.
And do you remember the trumpet player, the trombone player, any of them?

Well, we had different trumpet players that went through in that three or four years. Even Rene LeWap went through it for a while. Oh. Your current day popular Rene LeWap who plays all these carnival balls and does a wonderful job. Rene went through it for several months, maybe six or eight months. I don't recall how long each man stayed. A young fine trumpet man by the name of Walter Darwin played trumpet with us for a while and he was I think pretty active in the Lions Club lately or in the last few years. I haven't seen Walter in many years. But last time I saw him I think he was active in the Lions Club. He was a fine little trumpet man. I remember we going way back to 1929 or early 30. So I think that's the only two trumpet men I can recall but there were two or three others but I can't recall their names. It was too far back there.
And the trombone players you don't remember?

No. Well, we had, I don't know if, yeah, a boy by the name of Chatelaine played trombone with us at one time. Uh, I can't recall the others but there was probably one, maybe one other one. And a drummer?
A drummer. Did you tell me or not?

No, I can't recall who was on drums because we went through one or two drummers too. Yeah, well. Drummers and, uh, drummers I can't recall. Chatelaine was on trombone. Were you in the union then? Oh no, this is way before the union. We never joined the union until, uh, I think around 1939 I was with Al Streeman.
